destinations.terrain: Lift-served bike park and Nordic trail riding; all levels
destinations.pitch: Scandinavia's biggest bike park, on the slopes of Åreskutan, with dozens of lift-served trails and natural singletrack through birch and open fell.
destinations.weather: Long light evenings in summer; mosquitoes in July.

children.name: Åre Bike Park
children.note: Lift-served downhill, flow and jump lines

destinations.hireNote: The bike park and shops in the village rent downhill and trail bikes

destinations.name: Hafjell (Lillehammer)
destinations.terrain: Lift-served bike park and rooty forest trails; all levels
destinations.pitch: Norway's best-known bike park, on an Olympic ski hill above Lillehammer, with gondola-served flow and downhill and rooty Norwegian forest trails.

children.name: Hafjell Bike Park
children.note: Gondola-served flow, jump and downhill trails

destinations.hireNote: The bike park rents downhill and trail bikes

destinations.name: Bovec (Soča Valley)
destinations.terrain: Big, quiet mountain passes and old military mule tracks; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: An emerald river valley under the Julian Alps, with the Vršič and Mangart road climbs, First World War mule tracks for mountain bikes, and rafting on the Soča.

children.name: Mangart Road
children.note: Slovenia's highest road, to ~2,050 m

children.name: Vršič Pass
children.note: Cobbled hairpins to 1,611 m

destinations.hireNote: A few outfitters rent mountain and e-bikes; road bikes are scarcer

destinations.name: Liège (Ardennes)
destinations.terrain: Short, steep climbs on rolling forest roads; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: The hills of Liège–Bastogne–Liège, the oldest of the Classics: short, steep climbs like La Redoute through forest and river valleys.

children.name: Côte de La Redoute
children.note: ~1.6 km at ~9.5%; steep and famous

children.name: Côte de la Roche-aux-Faucons
children.note: Steep and close to the finish of the Classic

destinations.hireNote: A few shops rent road bikes; many riders bring their own

destinations.name: Gran Canaria
destinations.terrain: Long climbs on quiet mountain roads from the coast; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: A winter training island like Tenerife, with warm coastal resorts and long, steep climbs into the volcanic interior, up to Pico de las Nieves at nearly 1,950 m.

children.name: Pico de las Nieves
children.note: From sea level to ~1,950 m

children.name: Soria
children.note: Steep, quiet climb past reservoirs

destinations.hireNote: Plenty of shops in the southern resorts renting road bikes

destinations.name: Annecy
destinations.terrain: Lake roads and big Alpine climbs; all levels
destinations.pitch: A lake town with a flat, car-free cycle path along the water and Tour de France climbs straight from the shore: the Col de la Forclaz, the Semnoz and the Aravis passes.

children.name: Col de la Forclaz de Montmin
children.note: Steep, with paragliders launching from the top

children.name: Semnoz
children.note: ~18 km to ~1,700 m above the lake

children.name: Col des Aravis
children.note: Classic pass toward Mont Blanc

destinations.hireNote: Plenty of shops renting road and e-bikes around the lake

destinations.name: San Sebastián (Basque Country)
destinations.terrain: Steep green hills and coastal roads; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: A food capital on the Bay of Biscay, with short, savage climbs like Jaizkibel above the sea and a Basque cycling culture that fills the roadsides on race days.
destinations.weather: Green for a reason: rain is likely in any month.

children.name: Jaizkibel
children.note: ~8 km above the sea; a Clásica San Sebastián classic

destinations.hireNote: Several shops renting road bikes

destinations.name: Granada (Sierra Nevada)
destinations.terrain: One of Europe's biggest road climbs, and dry, sunny back roads; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: Granada, home of the Alhambra, sits at the foot of one of the longest climbs in Europe: the road up the Sierra Nevada toward the Pico Veleta, over 3,000 m and among the highest paved roads in Europe.
destinations.weather: Summer is very hot in Granada; the top is snowbound from about November to May.

children.name: Pico Veleta
children.note: ~42 km and ~2,600 m of climbing from Granada; closed to cars above ~2,500 m

destinations.hireNote: A few shops in Granada rent road bikes

destinations.name: Heiligenblut (Grossglockner)
destinations.terrain: A famous toll road with long, steady hairpin climbs; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: The Grossglockner High Alpine Road climbs past Austria's highest peak and the Pasterze glacier, with long climbs from both sides of the Hohe Tauern.
destinations.weather: The high road is usually open from May to early November.

children.name: Hochtor
children.note: Road summit at ~2,500 m; long climbs from both sides

children.name: Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe
children.note: Spur to the glacier viewpoint

destinations.hireNote: A few shops in the valleys, mostly e-bikes

destinations.name: Nicolosi (Etna)
destinations.terrain: Long volcano climbs through lava fields; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: Climb an active volcano from the sea: several roads wind up through orchards, pine and black lava fields to the Rifugio Sapienza near 1,900 m, a Giro d'Italia summit finish.
destinations.weather: Summer is hot at the bottom; eruptions occasionally close the upper roads.

children.name: Etna from Nicolosi
children.note: ~20 km to Rifugio Sapienza at ~1,900 m

destinations.hireNote: A few shops in Catania and the Etna villages rent road bikes

destinations.name: Raid Pyrénéen
destinations.airport: Biarritz near the start (Hendaye); Perpignan near the end (Cerbère)
destinations.terrain: Mountain roads over 18 cols; advanced
destinations.pitch: Atlantic to Mediterranean across the French Pyrenees, over 18 cols including the Aubisque, Tourmalet and Aspin. The classic challenge is to finish within 100 hours.
destinations.hireNote: No one-way hire; bring your own or go with a tour company

destinations.name: Transalp (Garmisch to Lake Garda)
destinations.airport: Munich ~1.5 h to the start; Verona ~1.5 h from Riva
destinations.terrain: Gravel tracks, mule paths and high passes; intermediate to advanced, with some pushing
destinations.pitch: The classic alpine crossing by mountain bike, from Bavaria over the Austrian and Italian Alps to Lake Garda, on well-known routes like the Albrecht and Joe routes.
destinations.hireNote: Tour companies hire bikes and move luggage; otherwise bring your own

destinations.name: Via Claudia Augusta
destinations.terrain: Cycle paths and quiet roads over the Reschen Pass; easy to intermediate
destinations.pitch: Follow an old Roman road from the Danube in Bavaria over the Fern and Reschen passes and down through the apple orchards of the Adige valley to Verona, mostly on traffic-free paths.
destinations.hireNote: One-way hire with luggage transfers is easy to arrange

destinations.name: Lake Constance loop
destinations.airport: Zurich ~1 h; Friedrichshafen is on the lake
destinations.terrain: Flat lakeside cycle paths; easy
destinations.pitch: A flat, easy loop around one of Europe's biggest lakes, through three countries, with vineyards, island gardens and ferries to skip a section.
destinations.hireNote: Plenty of hire around the lake, including one-way and e-bikes

destinations.name: Hebridean Way
destinations.airport: Ferry from Oban to Barra (start); ferry from Stornoway (end)
destinations.terrain: Quiet single-track roads, causeways and two ferries; easy to intermediate, but windy
destinations.pitch: Ten islands linked by causeways and ferries, from Vatersay to the Butt of Lewis: white-sand beaches, Gaelic villages and standing stones, and a lot of wind.
destinations.hireNote: A couple of shops on the islands; no one-way hire

destinations.name: Coast to Coast (C2C)
destinations.airport: Whitehaven or Workington (start); Sunderland or Tynemouth (end)
destinations.terrain: Lanes, cycle paths and some rough tracks over the Pennines; intermediate
destinations.pitch: Britain's most popular long-distance ride, from the Irish Sea through the northern Lake District and over the Pennines to the North Sea.
destinations.hireNote: Local companies hire bikes and bring them back from the finish

destinations.name: Highland Trail 550
destinations.terrain: Rough singletrack, bog and river crossings with hike-a-bike; very advanced
destinations.pitch: A tough, self-supported loop through the wildest parts of the Scottish Highlands on stalkers' paths and old drove roads, with long hike-a-bike sections and few places to resupply.
destinations.weather: Midges in summer; river crossings can be impassable after rain.
destinations.hireNote: Set up for rough bikepacking

destinations.name: Camino de Santiago
destinations.airport: Biarritz ~1 h to the start; Santiago airport at the end
destinations.terrain: Dirt pilgrim paths and quiet roads; intermediate
destinations.pitch: The medieval pilgrim way across northern Spain (the Camino Francés), through Pamplona, Burgos and León and over the Galician hills to Santiago, with cheap pilgrim hostels all the way. Bikes can follow the paths or the parallel roads.
destinations.weather: The Meseta is hot in July and August; Galicia is often wet.
destinations.hireNote: Several companies hire bikes one way and collect them in Santiago

destinations.name: Valle de Bravo
destinations.terrain: Pine-forest singletrack on old volcanoes, from cross-country loops to steep descents; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: A lakeside colonial town in pine-covered hills, with forest singletrack in the Monte Alto park on the edge of town and local guides who know the steeper descents.
destinations.weather: The rainy season runs from June to September.

children.name: Monte Alto
children.note: Volcano-slope loops in the state park above town

destinations.hireNote: Guided-ride operators supply bikes; there's no obvious rental shop, so many riders bring their own

destinations.name: Medellín
destinations.terrain: Long climbs on mountain roads in spring-like weather; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: The 'city of eternal spring', in a country mad about cycling: mild weather all year, long climbs out of the valley in every direction, and car-free roads on Sunday mornings.
destinations.weather: Two rainier seasons, roughly April–May and October–November.

children.name: Alto de Las Palmas
children.note: ~15.5 km and ~950 m at ~6% out of the city

destinations.hireNote: Several shops and tour companies rent road bikes

destinations.name: Cusco (Sacred Valley)
destinations.airport: Cusco ~15 min; Lima ~1.5 h by air
destinations.terrain: High-altitude singletrack on old Inca paths and dirt roads; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: Ride old Inca paths and dirt roads above 3,000 m over the Sacred Valley, past terraces and ruins, with long descents to the river.
destinations.weather: The rainy season is November to March, and the altitude takes a few days to get used to.

children.name: Sacred Valley descents
children.note: Long descents from the high plains down to the river

destinations.hireNote: Tour operators in Cusco rent bikes, usually with a guide

destinations.name: Bariloche
destinations.airport: Bariloche ~20 min; Buenos Aires ~2 h by air
destinations.terrain: Lakeside forest singletrack and lift-served descents; all levels
destinations.pitch: A lake town in Argentine Patagonia with forest singletrack, lift-served riding at Cerro Catedral in summer, and the Circuito Chico road loop past lakes and mountains.
destinations.weather: It's often windy; summer is short but long-lit.

children.name: Cerro Catedral
children.note: Lift-served descents in summer

destinations.hireNote: Several shops rent mountain and road bikes

destinations.name: Lagunas Route
destinations.region: Uyuni to San Pedro de Atacama
destinations.airport: Uyuni (start), San Pedro de Atacama in Chile (end)
destinations.terrain: Sand, washboard and rock at high altitude; advanced, very remote
destinations.pitch: Across Bolivia's high desert from the Uyuni salt flats past flamingo lagoons, geysers and volcanoes to Chile's Atacama, mostly above 4,000 m.
destinations.weather: Freezing nights and strong afternoon winds; the salt flats can flood in the wet season.
destinations.hireNote: Hire in Uyuni is basic; most riders bring their own

destinations.name: Knysna (Garden Route)
destinations.terrain: Forest singletrack and coastal trails; all levels
destinations.pitch: Indigenous forest singletrack along the Garden Route, with lagoons, beaches and whale-watching between rides.

children.name: Harkerville
children.note: Classic forest and coastal loops

destinations.hireNote: Outeniqua Bike Hire by the Harkerville trails rents adult bikes; book ahead

destinations.name: Nizwa (Jebel Akhdar)
destinations.terrain: Very steep mountain roads and empty desert roads; advanced
destinations.pitch: Empty, smooth roads through desert and date-palm oases, and the brutal Green Mountain climb, a Tour of Oman summit finish averaging over 10%.
destinations.weather: Summer is dangerously hot.

children.name: Jebel Akhdar
children.note: The Tour of Oman finishes ~6 km up at ~10%; the road keeps climbing for twice as far

destinations.hireNote: A few shops in Muscat rent road bikes

destinations.name: Fujiyoshida (Mount Fuji)
destinations.terrain: Big volcano climbs and lake loops; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: Loop the Fuji Five Lakes and climb the Fuji Subaru Line toward the fifth station at about 2,300 m, the course of the Mt Fuji Hill Climb race.
destinations.weather: The rainy season is June; the upper road closes in winter.

children.name: Fuji Subaru Line
children.note: ~25 km and ~1,300 m to the fifth station at ~2,300 m; bikes pay a small toll

destinations.hireNote: Plenty of city and e-bikes around Lake Kawaguchi; road bikes are harder to find

destinations.name: Chiang Mai
destinations.airport: Chiang Mai ~15 min; Bangkok ~1 h by air
destinations.terrain: Steep jungle climbs and singletrack; all levels
destinations.pitch: A relaxed city in Thailand's northern hills, with steep road climbs like Doi Suthep and Doi Inthanon, jungle singletrack and cheap living.
destinations.weather: Rainy from May to October; smoky haze in March and April.

children.name: Doi Suthep
children.note: ~11 km at ~6% from the edge of the city to the temple

children.name: Doi Inthanon
children.note: Thailand's highest road; very steep near the top

destinations.hireNote: Several shops rent road and mountain bikes

destinations.name: Manali to Leh
destinations.airport: Manali (start; Kullu airport ~1.5 h), Leh (end; flights to Delhi)
destinations.terrain: High mountain road with rough sections and passes over 5,000 m; advanced
destinations.pitch: One of the world's highest roads, over several passes above 5,000 m, from the green Kullu valley to the high desert of Ladakh.
destinations.weather: Open roughly June to September; altitude sickness is a real risk.
destinations.hireNote: Tour operators in Manali hire bikes for supported trips; otherwise bring your own

destinations.name: Bright (Victorian Alps)
destinations.terrain: Long alpine climbs and forest mountain-bike trails; all levels
destinations.pitch: A country town under the Victorian Alps with Australia's biggest road climbs (Mount Buffalo, Hotham and Falls Creek), plus mountain-bike trails and rail trails.

children.name: Mount Buffalo
children.note: ~20 km at ~5%

children.name: Mount Hotham
children.note: ~30 km and ~1,300 m from Harrietville; steep in places

children.name: Mystic MTB Park
children.note: Shuttled trails just outside town

destinations.hireNote: Several shops renting road, mountain and e-bikes

destinations.name: Adelaide
destinations.terrain: Hills, vineyards and quiet roads; all levels
destinations.pitch: The home of the Tour Down Under, with climbs straight out of the city into the Adelaide Hills, McLaren Vale wine country and Willunga Hill to the south.
destinations.weather: Summer heatwaves can top 40°C.

children.name: Willunga Hill
children.note: ~3 km at ~7.5%; the Tour Down Under decider

children.name: Norton Summit
children.note: Classic climb from the city into the hills

destinations.hireNote: Several shops renting road bikes

destinations.name: Cairns
destinations.terrain: Steep rainforest singletrack and purpose-built flow; intermediate to expert
destinations.pitch: Tropical rainforest riding, from the steep Smithfield trails that have hosted World Cups and World Championships to the purpose-built network at Atherton in the cooler highlands.
destinations.weather: The wet season, December to April, brings heavy rain and heat.

children.name: Smithfield
children.note: Steep, rooty rainforest trails

children.name: Atherton
children.note: ~1.5 h: purpose-built flow in the cooler highlands

destinations.hireNote: A few shops rent trail bikes

destinations.name: Otago Central Rail Trail
destinations.terrain: Gentle gravel rail trail over viaducts and through tunnels; easy
destinations.pitch: New Zealand's original great ride: a gentle gravel rail trail through the gold-rush country of Central Otago, with old viaducts, tunnels and country pubs.
destinations.hireNote: Plenty of operators hire bikes one way and move luggage

destinations.name: Munda Biddi Trail
destinations.terrain: Forest singletrack and gravel; intermediate
destinations.pitch: One of the world's longest purpose-built off-road cycle trails, through jarrah and karri forest from the hills behind Perth to the south coast, with free campsites a day's ride apart.
destinations.weather: Summer is hot and dry, with fire closures.
destinations.hireNote: Set up for bikepacking

destinations.name: Fernie
destinations.terrain: Steep, rooty forest singletrack and a lift-served bike park; intermediate to expert
destinations.pitch: A Rockies town ringed by trails, with long forest climbs and descents on Mount Fernie and lift-served downhill at Fernie Alpine Resort.

children.name: Fernie Alpine Resort
children.note: Lift-served park with ~35 trails, green to double black; late June to Labour Day

children.name: Mount Fernie
children.note: Big network of forest singletrack from town

destinations.hireNote: Several shops in town and at the resort rent bikes

destinations.name: Rossland
destinations.terrain: Long, natural alpine singletrack and a new lift-served park; intermediate to expert
destinations.pitch: A small mountain town and old gold-mining camp with big natural singletrack, including the Seven Summits ridge, an IMBA Epic, and a lift-served bike park at Red Mountain that opened in 2025.

children.name: Seven Summits Trail
children.note: ~30 km of ridge singletrack, ridden north to south; best July to early October

children.name: RED Bike Park
children.note: Lift-served park at Red Mountain, new in 2025

destinations.hireNote: A couple of shops in town, and a rental shop at the base of Red Mountain

destinations.name: Revelstoke
destinations.terrain: Gondola-served alpine flow and tech, plus town trail networks; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: A railway town in the Selkirks with a growing gondola-served bike park on Mount Mackenzie, including the long Fifty-six Twenty descent, and forest trail networks just out of town.

children.name: Revelstoke Mountain Resort
children.note: Gondola-served flow, tech and jump trails; mostly intermediate and up

children.name: Mount Macpherson
children.note: Forest singletrack just south of town

destinations.hireNote: Shops in town and at the resort rent bike-park and trail bikes

destinations.name: Cumberland
destinations.terrain: Loamy, rooty forest singletrack; all levels
destinations.pitch: An old coal-mining village on Vancouver Island with more than 200 km of hand-built forest singletrack starting at the edge of town, one of the busiest trail networks in North America.
destinations.weather: Rideable most of the year, but wet from November to March.

children.name: Cumberland Community Forest
children.note: 200+ km of trails from the village

destinations.hireNote: A couple of shops in the village rent trail bikes

destinations.name: Vallnord (Pal Arinsal)
destinations.airport: Andorra–La Seu d'Urgell ~30 min; Barcelona or Toulouse ~3 h
destinations.terrain: Lift-served downhill, enduro and flow on ski slopes; all levels
destinations.pitch: A lift-served bike park in the Pyrenees that has hosted World Cups and the 2015 World Championships, with 60+ km of trails and big mountain views.

children.name: Pal Arinsal Bike Park
children.note: Chairlifts to 2,350 m; downhill, enduro and a beginner zone

destinations.hireNote: Bike-park and e-bikes for hire at the resort and in La Massana

destinations.name: Nelson
destinations.terrain: Forest singletrack from town and shuttled backcountry trails; all levels
destinations.pitch: A sunny small city with trails starting from the centre, the Coppermine Trail over the hills behind it, and the shuttled Wairoa Gorge an hour away.

children.name: Codgers
children.note: Loops minutes from the city centre

children.name: Coppermine Trail
children.note: ~40 km Great Ride circuit over Coppermine Saddle; grade 4

children.name: Wairoa Gorge
children.note: ~1 h: 70+ km of hand-built singletrack with 4WD shuttles

destinations.hireNote: Several shops rent trail and e-bikes

destinations.name: Oakridge
destinations.terrain: Long, loamy shuttled descents through old-growth forest; intermediate to advanced
destinations.pitch: A small timber town in the Cascades and an IMBA gold-level Ride Center, with long shuttled descents through old-growth forest like the Alpine Trail.
destinations.weather: Wildfire smoke and closures are possible in late summer.

children.name: Alpine Trail
children.note: Shuttle up, then ~1,400 m of descent through big trees

children.name: Waldo Lake Loop
children.note: ~31 km IMBA Epic around a clear alpine lake

destinations.hireNote: Local outfits rent bikes and run daily shuttles; more choice in Eugene

destinations.name: Duluth
destinations.terrain: Rocky, rooty singletrack and a lift-served park, inside the city; all levels
destinations.pitch: A port city on Lake Superior and an IMBA gold-level Ride Center, with the Duluth Traverse linking trail parks right across town and lift-served riding at Spirit Mountain.
destinations.weather: Snow lingers into May; autumn colour peaks in late September.

children.name: Duluth Traverse
children.note: ~65 km of linked singletrack end to end across the city

children.name: Spirit Mountain
children.note: Lift-served downhill and flow

destinations.hireNote: A few shops rent trail bikes

destinations.name: Thredbo
destinations.terrain: Lift-served downhill, flow and long all-mountain trails; all levels
destinations.pitch: Australia's highest lift-served riding, under Mount Kosciuszko: the Cannonball downhill, the beginner-friendly Kosciuszko Flow and the long All-Mountain Trail, all from the chairlift.

children.name: Thredbo MTB Park
children.note: Chairlift-served Cannonball, Flow and All-Mountain trails

destinations.hireNote: Bike-park and trail bikes for hire in the village

destinations.name: Dalton Highway (Haul Road)
destinations.airport: Fairbanks (start), Deadhorse on the Arctic Ocean (end; fly out)
destinations.terrain: Mostly gravel truck road with long hills and one big pass; intermediate, very remote
destinations.pitch: The truck road to the Arctic oil fields: about 800 km from Fairbanks across the Yukon River and the Arctic Circle, over the Brooks Range at Atigun Pass and out across the tundra of the North Slope. Services are very few and far apart.
destinations.weather: Mosquitoes in June and July; snow is possible at Atigun Pass in any month, and trucks throw dust and stones.
destinations.hireNote: There's nothing along the road; bring everything

destinations.name: Dempster Highway
destinations.region: Dawson City to Inuvik, Yukon and NWT
destinations.airport: Dawson City (start; Whitehorse ~6 h), Inuvik (end), or on to Tuktoyaktuk
destinations.terrain: Gravel highway across tundra and two mountain ranges; intermediate, very remote
destinations.pitch: Canada's road to the Arctic: gravel nearly all the way from near Dawson City through Tombstone park, across the Arctic Circle and the Richardson Mountains to Inuvik, with a newer road on to the Arctic Ocean at Tuktoyaktuk. No services for the first 365 km.
destinations.weather: Mud after rain, mosquitoes in midsummer, and grizzlies along the road.
destinations.hireNote: There's nothing along the road; bring everything

destinations.name: Silk Road Mountain Race route
destinations.airport: Bishkek; start and finish change each year
destinations.terrain: Dirt roads, jeep tracks and hike-a-bike over high passes; very advanced
destinations.pitch: A roughly 1,900 km unsupported route through Kyrgyzstan's Tian Shan, over high passes, past yurt camps and alpine lakes, with about 80% off pavement. The route changes each year, and you can ride it outside the race.
destinations.weather: Cold nights at altitude, river crossings and few places to resupply.
destinations.hireNote: Set up for rough, remote bikepacking

destinations.name: Karakoram Highway
destinations.terrain: Paved mountain highway with landslide sections; advanced and remote
destinations.pitch: One of the world's great mountain roads, up the Indus and Hunza valleys under Nanga Parbat and Rakaposhi, through Hunza's orchards to the Khunjerab Pass on the Chinese border at about 4,700 m.
destinations.weather: Check current security advice before going; landslides can close the road.
destinations.hireNote: Tour operators supply bikes on supported trips; otherwise bring your own

destinations.name: Annapurna Circuit
destinations.region: Besisahar to Pokhara via the Thorong La
destinations.airport: Kathmandu ~6 h by road to Besisahar; Pokhara at the end
destinations.terrain: Jeep roads and singletrack with a long carry over a 5,416 m pass; advanced
destinations.pitch: Ride around the Annapurna massif on jeep roads and old trekking trails, pushing and carrying the bike over the Thorong La at 5,416 m, then a long, technical descent to Muktinath and down the Kali Gandaki gorge. Teahouses all the way.
destinations.weather: The monsoon runs June to September, and the pass can be snowbound in winter.
destinations.hireNote: Mountain bikes for hire in Kathmandu and Pokhara, and in Jomsom and Muktinath for the descent

destinations.name: Tour Aotearoa
destinations.airport: Auckland ~6 h to Cape Reinga (start); Invercargill near Bluff (end)
destinations.terrain: Gravel trails, quiet roads, a beach and boat crossings; intermediate, long
destinations.pitch: The length of New Zealand on its Great Rides and back roads, from Cape Reinga to Bluff, including a ride along 90 Mile Beach at low tide, forest trails and boat crossings.
destinations.hireNote: Set up for long-distance bikepacking

destinations.name: TransAmerica Trail
destinations.airport: Astoria (west end; Portland ~2 h), Yorktown (east end; Norfolk ~45 min)
destinations.terrain: Rural two-lane roads across ten states and the Rockies; intermediate, very long
destinations.pitch: America's classic coast-to-coast ride, mapped for the 1976 bicentennial: about 6,800 km through the Cascades, Yellowstone, the Rockies, the plains, the Ozarks and the Appalachians.
destinations.hireNote: No one-way hire

destinations.name: Old Ghost Road

destinations.terrain: Hand-built backcountry singletrack; advanced (grade 4)
destinations.pitch: A gold miners' road that was never finished, now singletrack across the mountains of the West Coast, with booked huts in spectacular spots like Ghost Lake.
destinations.weather: Snow is possible on the tops; sandflies lower down.
destinations.hireNote: Shuttle operators at both ends can arrange bikes; most riders bring their own

destinations.name: Jackson & Teton Valley
destinations.airport: Jackson Hole airport ~15 min; Idaho Falls ~2 h
destinations.terrain: Two lift-served bike parks plus steep, rooty mountain singletrack; all levels
destinations.pitch: An IMBA Ride Center on both sides of the Tetons, with lift-served bike parks at Jackson Hole and Grand Targhee and steep, volunteer-built descents off Teton Pass.

children.name: Jackson Hole Mountain Resort
children.note: Lift-served flow, jump and tech trails at Teton Village

children.name: Teton Pass
children.note: Steep, technical downhill trails; no lift, so pedal or shuttle up

children.name: Grand Targhee
children.note: Lift-served park and the Grand Targhee Loop, an IMBA Epic

destinations.hireNote: Rentals at Jackson Hole, Grand Targhee and shops in Jackson and Driggs

destinations.name: Snowshoe

destinations.pitch: Iceland's famous hiking trail, ridden across rhyolite mountains, black lava sand and glacier rivers between Landmannalaugar and Þórsmörk, then over the Fimmvörðuháls pass between two glaciers to Skógar. It's an IMBA Epic.
destinations.weather: Expect long push-and-carry sections on steep, loose climbs, snowfields and the Fimmvörðuháls pass. Busy with hikers in July and August, so ride early or late; it's a protected area, and you can only camp at the huts.
